message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on a man's jacket and pants that zip together into a protective set. The fabric is 50% Kermel (polyamide-imide, a synthetic fiber), 39% Lenzing FR (flame-resistant viscose, an artificial fiber), 10% para-aramid, and 1% carbon. Synthetic fibers are the largest share, at 60% when the para-aramid is counted with them.

The question is whether the two garments form a "suit" or a "ski-suit"-type set, or whether they are classified separately. Because the jacket and pants zip together, they may be treated as a set for tariff purposes. Heading 6211 covers track suits, ski-suits, and other garments, and the 6211.33 subheadings cover men's garments of man-made fibers. Heading 6203 covers men's suits, but a suit requires the jacket to be lined, and this jacket is unlined, so it does not qualify as a suit under 6203.

Heading 6211 does not apply to separate garments of this kind. The classification would therefore be jacket in 6201 and pants in 6203. A protective garment that is woven and made of man-made fibers would fall under 6201.93 for a jacket and 6203.43 for pants. Because the garments are worn together and zipped, they could be classified under 6211.33.9010 as "other garments, men's, of man-made fibers."

The question asks for a single code, so I will choose 6211.33.9060, the men's other garments of man-made fibers. I'm not certain of the statistical suffix, though. The 6211.33.90 line has several suffixes, including 6211.33.9010 for "Other: Other: Coveralls and overalls" and 6211.33.9060 for "Other."

Instead I'll go with 6211.33.9060, which is the likeliest choice.
